functions.name: BG_StringHashValue
functions.evidence: Case-insensitive position-weighted string hash (sum of tolower(c) * (i + 0x77), -1 mapped to 0). Evidence: id Tech BG_StringHashValue counterpart; used by every BG_*IndexForString lookup in this chunk.

functions.name: BG_AnimParseError
functions.evidence: Formats the message into a 1024 byte buffer and raises a drop error, adding the script name and parse line while mp/playeranim.script is being parsed (g_08184860 non-null). Evidence: every "BG_..." parse-error string in this chunk goes through it.

functions.name: BG_AnimationIndexForString
functions.evidence: Looks the animation name up (hash then Q_stricmp). Without a name table it scans the animation array; with a name table (g_0860e4a8) it scans/extends that table via Scr_AddAnimTreeEntry. Evidence: string "BG_AnimationIndexForString: unknown player animation '%s'" at 0x081527c0.

functions.name: BG_AnimationForString
functions.evidence: Returns the animation_t whose name matches, or raises an error and returns 0. Evidence: string "BG_AnimationForString: unknown player animation '%s'" at 0x08152820.

functions.name: BG_IndexForString
functions.signature: int BG_IndexForString(const char *token, struct animStringItem_t *strings, int allowFail);
functions.evidence: Finds a token in a { string, hash } table that ends with a null string; computes missing hashes lazily. On a miss it errors unless allowFail is set and returns -1. Evidence: string "BG_IndexForString: unknown token '%s'" at 0x08152860.

functions.name: BG_CopyStringIntoBuffer
functions.signature: char *BG_CopyStringIntoBuffer(const char *string, char *buffer, unsigned int bufferSize, int *offset);
functions.evidence: Appends a string to a fixed buffer (offset advanced past the terminator) and returns its address. Evidence: string "BG_CopyStringIntoBuffer: out of buffer space" at 0x081528a0.

functions.name: BG_SetPlayerAnimTypeName
functions.evidence: Stores a PLAYERANIMTYPE name and its hash in g_08626b80[index] (the table referenced as the string list of condition 0 in g_08184c60). Called for each entry by fn_080f2be2.

functions.name: BG_ClearPlayerAnimTypeNames
functions.evidence: Clears the 128 entry PLAYERANIMTYPE name table and re-registers the names (fn_080f2be2 calls BG_SetPlayerAnimTypeName for every loaded weapon anim type).

functions.name: BG_AnimNameEntryForIndex
functions.evidence: Returns the name-table entry whose id equals the animation index, or 0 when absent. Errors when the index is not below the animation count. Evidence: string "Player animation index %i out of 0 to %i range" at 0x081528e0.

functions.name: BG_ClearAnimReferencedFlags
functions.evidence: Clears animation_t::referenced for all animations, then (non multiplayer only) marks every animation named by a command of scriptEvents[10]. Called at the end of BG_LoadAnim.

functions.name: BG_LoadAnim
functions.evidence: Builds animations[] from the loaded animation tree: entry 0 is "root", unreferenced slots are "unused", real animations get name/hash/duration (ms, min 500)/moveSpeed (delta length per second) and the looping flag, then runs BG_AnimParseAnimScript and BG_ClearAnimReferencedFlags. Evidence: strings "root" / "unused"; calls the parser and the referenced-flag clear.

functions.name: BG_ParseConditionBits
functions.signature: void BG_ParseConditionBits(const char **text, struct animStringItem_t *stringTable, int conditionIndex, unsigned int *result);
functions.evidence: Parses one comma-terminated condition expression ("a AND b NOT c", "none", "all", "MINUS"/"NOT") from the current line into a 64-bit mask. Words resolve first against the script-defined values (g_0860dba0/g_0860e020) and then against the condition's string table. Only the first dword of result is cleared on entry; the local mask persists between terms (quirks preserved). Evidence: strings "BG_ParseConditionBits: unexpected end of condition" and "...: unexpected '%s'".

functions.name: BG_ParseConditions
functions.evidence: Parses the condition list of one script item up to "default" or end of line. Each condition name resolves through g_08184c00; bit-flag conditions go to BG_ParseConditionBits, value conditions read one more token. The two value dwords persist across conditions (stale value[1] for value type). Evidence: strings "BG_ParseConditions: no conditions found" and "...expected condition value...".

functions.name: BG_ParseCommands
functions.signature: void BG_ParseCommands(const char **text, struct animScriptItem_t *item, struct animScriptData_t *data);
functions.evidence: Parses the command block of one script item: "<bodypart> <animation> [duration n] [turretanim] [blendtime n]" pairs (a second part unless the first is 'both'), then "sound <alias>" entries, until the closing brace (which is pushed back). While not collecting names (g_0860e4a8 == 0) it also updates animation_t move-type bits, flags and blend times. Evidence: strings "BG_ParseCommands: expected animation", "...unknown parameter '%s'" etc.

functions.name: BG_AnimParseAnimScript
functions.signature: void BG_AnimParseAnimScript(struct animScriptData_t *data, struct animNameEntry_t *animNames, int *numAnimNames);
functions.evidence: Parses mp/playeranim.script (loaded once into g_0860e4c0) into scriptData: sections "defines" (set <type> <name> = <bits>), "animations", "canned_animations", "statechanges" and "events". Depth/stack bookkeeping: depth 0 = section level, then state / move type / item / commands. The "unexpected end of file" error is raised with a format that has %s but no argument (as in the binary). While parsing, g_0860b424/g_0860e4a8/g_0860e4ac are set; g_08184860 is cleared at the end. Evidence: strings "BG_AnimParseAnimScript", "mp/playeranim.script" (g_08184860), many "BG_AnimParseAnimScript: ..." errors.

functions.name: BG_EvaluateConditions
functions.evidence: Returns 1 when every condition of the item matches the client's condition values: bit-flag conditions need a shared bit (low or high dword), value conditions need equality. Evidence: id Tech BG_EvaluateConditions counterpart; reads the g_08184c60 type per condition.

functions.name: BG_FirstValidItem
functions.evidence: Returns the first item of the script whose conditions match the client's current condition values (g_0860b420 client table), or 0. Evidence: id Tech BG_FirstValidItem counterpart.

functions.name: BG_PlayAnim
functions.signature: int BG_PlayAnim(struct playerState_s *ps, unsigned int animIndex, int bodyPart, int forceDuration, int setTimer, int isContinue, int force);
functions.evidence: Starts an animation on legs (body part 1), torso (2) or both (3) of the player state. Duration is the animation duration + 50 ms unless forced. Returns the legs duration when the legs part was (re)started, otherwise -1. For 'both' the torso part is started with animation index 0 (quirk). Evidence: id Tech BG_PlayAnim counterpart (ps legs/torso anim + timer toggling bit 0x200).

functions.name: BG_PlayAnimName
functions.signature: void BG_PlayAnimName(struct playerState_s *ps, const char *animName, int bodyPart, int setTimer, int isContinue, int force);
functions.evidence: BG_PlayAnim by animation name (result discarded, forceDuration 0).

functions.name: BG_ExecuteCommand
functions.signature: int BG_ExecuteCommand(struct playerState_s *ps, struct animCommand_t *command, int setTimer, int isContinue, int force);
functions.evidence: Executes one script command: plays each of its two parts with the part-0 duration + 50 ms (the second part also tests bodyPart[0], not bodyPart[1], when choosing the result path), then triggers the sound callback. Returns the duration when a legs/both part started, otherwise -1. Evidence: id Tech BG_ExecuteCommand counterpart; sound callback at animScriptData + 0xb3bc4.

functions.name: BG_AnimScriptAnimation
functions.signature: unsigned int BG_AnimScriptAnimation(struct playerState_s *ps, int state, int moveType, int isContinue);
functions.evidence: Plays the movement animation for (state, moveType): walks down from the given state to the first state whose script has a matching item, sets condition 3 (MOVETYPE) and executes the command picked by clientNum modulo the command count. Returns 1/0 (started or not) or -1 when nothing applies. Evidence: id Tech BG_AnimScriptAnimation counterpart; scriptAnims[state][moveType] indexing.

functions.name: BG_AnimScriptStateChange
functions.signature: int BG_AnimScriptStateChange(struct playerState_s *ps, int toState, int fromState);
functions.evidence: Runs the state-change script (fromState -> toState): first matching item, random command. Returns the command duration or -1. Evidence: id Tech BG_AnimScriptStateChange counterpart; scriptStateChange[from][to] indexing.

functions.name: BG_AnimScriptEvent
functions.signature: int BG_AnimScriptEvent(struct playerState_s *ps, int event, int isContinue, int force);
functions.evidence: Runs the event script (pain, death, ...) for the player: first matching item, random command, timer set. Event 1 (DEATH) also runs for pm_type >= 6. Returns the duration or -1. Evidence: id Tech BG_AnimScriptEvent counterpart; scriptEvents[event]; 15 callers.

functions.name: BG_GetAnimString
functions.signature: struct animation_t *BG_GetAnimString(int unused, unsigned int index);
functions.evidence: Returns animations[index] of the parse target; errors when the index is out of range. Evidence: string "BG_GetAnimString: anim index is out of range" at 0x08153100.

functions.name: BG_UpdateConditionValue
functions.signature: void BG_UpdateConditionValue(int clientNum, int condition, int value, int checkConversion);
functions.evidence: Sets a client's animation condition: bit-flag conditions (type 0) with checkConversion get a single bit set in a cleared 64-bit mask, everything else stores the raw value in the low dword. Evidence: id Tech BG_UpdateConditionValue counterpart; table type at g_08184c60[condition].

functions.name: BG_GetConditionValue
functions.signature: unsigned int BG_GetConditionValue(struct clientInfo_s *client, int condition, int checkConversion);
functions.evidence: Reads a client's condition value; with checkConversion on a bit-flag condition it returns the index of the first set bit (0..63) instead, or 0 when no bit is set. Evidence: id Tech BG_GetConditionValue counterpart.

functions.name: BG_AnimScriptEventAnimIndex
functions.evidence: Like BG_AnimScriptEvent but only picks a random command of the first matching event item and returns its first animation index instead of executing it (-1 when none).

functions.name: BG_GetAnimationForIndex
functions.signature: struct animation_t *BG_GetAnimationForIndex(int unused, unsigned int index);
functions.evidence: Returns animations[index] of the parse target (g_0860b424); raises an error when out of range. Evidence: string "BG_GetAnimationForIndex: index out of bounds" at 0x08153140.

functions.name: BG_UpdateConditionsFromPmove
functions.evidence: Refreshes the animation conditions from the pmove: 0 PLAYERANIMTYPE and 1 WEAPONCLASS from the current weapon, 7 WEAPON_POSITION (eFlags 0x40000), 2 MOUNTED (eFlags 0x300), 4 UNDERHAND (ps field 0xe8 > 0), 6 FIRING (button bit 0). Evidence: condition names at g_08184c00 (index order); id Tech BG_UpdateConditionValue use.

functions.name: BG_AnimFlagsTestA
functions.signature: bool BG_AnimFlagsTestA(struct clientInfo_s *client, unsigned int animNumber);
functions.evidence: True when the animation's move-type mask intersects lo 0xc4 or hi 0x180 (animation number with the restart toggle bit 0x200 removed).

functions.name: BG_AnimFlagsTestB
functions.signature: bool BG_AnimFlagsTestB(struct clientInfo_s *client, unsigned int animNumber);
functions.evidence: True when the animation's low move-type mask intersects 0x308.

functions.name: BG_SetNewAnimation
functions.signature: void BG_SetNewAnimation(struct clientInfo_s *client, struct playerAnimLerp_t *lerp, unsigned int newAnimation, int isDeath);
functions.evidence: Switches a lerp frame (legs or torso of a client) to a new animation number: picks the blend time (170/250/120 ms defaults, never below the pending move-blend deadline), recomputes the run-cycle phase for moving animations and drives the animation tree (weights/times/roots). Legs updates do not touch the shared root animations; death animations (flag 0x40) must not loop. Evidence: string "death animation '%s' is looping" at 0x081531c0; id Tech CG_SetLerpFrameAnimation counterpart.

functions.name: BG_RunLerpFrame
functions.signature: void BG_RunLerpFrame(struct clientInfo_s *client, struct playerAnimLerp_t *lerp, unsigned int newAnimation, struct entityState_s *es);
functions.evidence: Per frame update of a lerp frame: starts a new animation when the number changed, then estimates the animation speed scale from the distance moved since the last snapshot (vertical distance only for run-speed flagged animations), clamps it (0.1 minimum, move-speed dependent maximum) and applies it to the tree animation. Evidence: id Tech CG_RunLerpFrame counterpart; calls BG_SetNewAnimation with eFlags bit 19.

functions.name: BG_ClearFinishedAnimation
functions.evidence: When the lerp frame's animation has finished (tree value 0), clears it and resets the blend time to 150 ms.

functions.name: BG_SwingAngles
functions.signature: void BG_SwingAngles(float destination, float swingTolerance, float clampTolerance, float speed, float *angle, int *swinging);
functions.evidence: Swings *angle toward the destination yaw/pitch: starts swinging when the difference exceeds the tolerance, moves by up to frameTime * max(0.5, |diff| * 0.05) * speed per call and clamps the final angle to within clampTolerance of the destination. Evidence: id Tech CG_SwingAngles counterpart (same parameter list and update rule).

functions.name: BG_PlayerAngles
functions.evidence: Computes the client's torso/legs yaw and torso pitch swing from the view angles and the entity's eFlags / MOVETYPE condition bits, calling BG_SwingAngles for torso yaw, legs yaw and torso pitch. Evidence: id Tech CG_PlayerAngles counterpart (legs/torso yaw swing, pitch * 0.6, 150 degree clamp).

open_questions: Client count of animScriptData_t.clients (stride 0x4b8 at +0xb3bfc) and the true size of animScriptData_t are not recovered; whether g_0860b420 and g_0860b424 always point to the same block is unknown.
The 19 callbacks Noop_080d6c32..ReturnZero_080d6cd4 are empty/return-0 stubs (likely abstract interface slots); their owners are in other chunks.
Semantics of the xanim calls fn_080c1c84/fn_080c2aa2/fn_080c1664 (weight, rate, flag arguments) and of fn_080c0daa/fn_080c0dee (current time/weight) are inferred only; callee chunks should name them.
BG_ExecuteCommand uses animDuration[0] and bodyPart[0] for the second part as well (kept as observed); unclear if intended.
The 'unexpected end of file' error in BG_AnimParseAnimScript passes no %s argument (reproduced); it prints stack garbage in the original.
